survivingClaim: Precise obstruction for five forms of positive-term sum rule on the prime stub chain: (i) the Littlewood window functional has coefficient side 0 at every stage for every unimodular chain (sigma > 0) and its bound-state term is a tail invariant bounded by the free inequality from below only; (ii) the mean form E + 4 pi delta = log zeta(2 sigma) is the classical density identity; (iii) at fixed stage no continuous functional of the phases separates zeta from U over window positions (Kronecker-Weyl, known, row Q21); (iv) the Simon-Zlatos difference condition holds for zeta on Re s > 0 and for THIN on Re s > b/2, so the coefficient condition is compatible with a zero at b to the right of the line; random U has infinite expected sum at sigma <= 1/2; (v) the H^2 point-evaluation step reaches only Re s > sigma_0 + 1/2 > 1 (known theorem). DH has no chain; the limit identity reads its off-line zero (0.0585171825 at sigma 0.75, 0.1085171825 at sigma 0.7). Not a theorem about all sum rules. No statement about zeros of zeta. One referee pass.
obstruction: Five forms: (i) window form = Littlewood's lemma, coefficient side 0 at every stage for every unimodular chain; the bound-state term is a tail invariant bounded from below only; (ii) mean form E + 4 pi delta = log zeta(2 sigma) is the classical density identity; (iii) at fixed stage no continuous functional of the phases separates zeta from U over window positions (Kronecker-Weyl, row Q21); (iv) the Simon-Zlatos difference condition holds for zeta on Re s > 0 and for THIN on Re s > b/2 with THIN's zero at b right of the line; (v) the H^2 point-evaluation step reaches only Re s > sigma_0 + 1/2 > 1. Not a theorem about all sum rules: a rule with identically vanishing coefficient side and a semicontinuous limit step is not covered, and that limit step is the target.

lesson: A sum-rule device outputs Lieb-Thirring (density) bounds; to give "no bound states" its coefficient side must vanish, and then its limit step is the target. Test any coefficient condition against THIN first: tail-thin sign changes keep every smoothness-in-delay condition while placing a zero right of the line.
